## Example 6.8 · Parts (c–d) {#iv6-example-6-8-cd .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .angles-lesson .a-dense}

```{=html}
<p>Three points <span data-math="P"></span>, <span data-math="Q"></span> and <span data-math="R"></span> have position vectors <span data-math="\mathbf p"></span>, <span data-math="\mathbf q"></span> and <span data-math="\mathbf r"></span> respectively, where</p><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\mathbf p=7\underset{\sim}{i}+10\underset{\sim}{j},\quad\mathbf q=3\underset{\sim}{i}+12\underset{\sim}{j},\quad\mathbf r=-\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}."></span></div><div class="a-cols "><div><p>c) Find the position vector of <span data-math="S"></span>, the midpoint of <span data-math="PR"></span>.</p><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="a-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show (c)</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{OS}=\frac{\mathbf p+\mathbf r}{2}=\begin{bmatrix}(7-1)/2\\(10+4)/2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\7\end{bmatrix}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{OS}=3\underset{\sim}{i}+7\underset{\sim}{j}"></span></div></div></div><div data-angles="triangle" class="a-figure"></div></div><div><p>d) Show that <span data-math="|\overrightarrow{QS}|=|\overrightarrow{RS}|"></span>. Using your previous results, or otherwise, find <span data-math="\angle PSQ"></span>.</p><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="a-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show (d)</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{QS}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\-5\end{bmatrix},\quad\overrightarrow{RS}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\3\end{bmatrix}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="|\overrightarrow{QS}|=5=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=|\overrightarrow{RS}|"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{SP}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\3\end{bmatrix},\quad\overrightarrow{SQ}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\5\end{bmatrix}"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\cos\angle PSQ=\frac{4(0)+3(5)}{5(5)}=\frac35"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\angle PSQ=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac35\right)\approx53.13^\circ"></span></div></div></div></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 6 · p. 47</div>

::: notes
The support diagram uses the actual coordinates and equal scales. Dot products at S require SP and SQ, not PS and SQ; reversing just one changes the angle to its supplement.
:::
